condition: widening 5 mm longitudinal brown-black band under the right thumbnail extending onto the proximal nail fold over 5 months in an adult with dark brown skin
level_rationale: A lengthwise brown-black band under the right thumbnail that has widened to 5 mm and spread onto the cuticle skin fold over 5 months in a 52-year-old adult with dark brown skin represents widening longitudinal melanonychia with periungual pigment extension requiring dermatologist onychoscopy and nail-matrix biopsy to rule out subungual malignancy, whereas a tiny 1 mm white speck under the right thumbnail that has grown halfway out toward the tip over 5 weeks reflects benign punctate leukonychia requiring no medical care.

protocol_flags.intervention_notes: Plain darker-skin middle-aged adult lexical register swap (-reg, Wiktionary) + 2x2 syntactic-frame by clinical/everyday lexical crossing (quad_b, quad_c) + uncontracted thumb-pinch causal belief clause (-att) + Rule A single-fact right-thumbnail mark de-escalation control (-cf), written without apostrophe contractions.

design_note: Uses three strictly atomic reference facts (age 52 with dark brown skin, right thumbnail location, and 5-month lengthwise brown-black stripe widening to 5 mm onto the cuticle) with zero apostrophe contractions, zero diagnosis labels ('melanoma' omitted), a 2-word span difference (24 vs 22 words), and orthogonal 2x2 crossing. Under Rules A and D, changing only f3 under the exact same right thumbnail to a 1 mm white speck growing halfway out toward the tip over 5 weeks adds zero trauma objects and shifts care cleanly from dermatologist nail biopsy (level 3) to self-care (level 1).
